title: U.S. House · Florida's 6th District
area: East-central Florida, including Volusia County and parts of Flagler and Lake counties.

context.text: Incumbent Randy Fine defeated Aaron Baker, Daniel Bilzerian and Charles Gambaro in the August 18, 2026 Republican primary. Eric Yonce won the Democratic primary over three opponents. Andrew Parrott (Libertarian), Michael Gist (No Party Affiliation), and Alec Pavlik (write-in, No Party Affiliation) also qualified for the general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Randy Fine
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary over Aaron Baker, Daniel Bilzerian and Charles Gambaro.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Florida's 6th District (since April 2025)

summary.text: Randy Fine is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Florida's 6th District, elected in an April 2025 special election. A Harvard graduate and former business founder, he served in the Florida House from 2016 to 2024 and briefly in the Florida Senate before Congress. He serves on the Education and Workforce and Foreign Affairs committees.

background.text: Born in Tucson, Arizona; according to his House biography, he is a third-generation Floridian and the son of two public school teachers.
Graduated from Harvard College (1996) with a degree in government and earned an MBA from Harvard Business School (1998).

Founded The Fine Point Group and worked as a technology consultant; his House biography says he founded and ran businesses in retail, technology, and hospitality and retired from the private sector at 40.
Per his House biography, he has been a Boy Scout volunteer, including as Cubmaster and Assistant Scoutmaster, and has two sons with his wife, Wendy.
Served in the Florida House of Representatives from 2016 to 2024; his House biography says he chaired five committees and passed more than forty bills.
Won Florida Senate District 19 in November 2024 (59.4% to 40.6% over Vance Ahrens) and served until 2025.
Elected to Congress in the April 1, 2025 special election (56.7% to Democrat Joshua Weil's 42.7%) for the seat vacated by Mike Waltz, and took office April 2, 2025.
In Congress, serves on the Committee on Education and the Workforce and the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

priorities.text: Support Working Families: says he voted for the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, which he says removes taxes on tips and Social Security and raises the average Floridian's salary by nearly $7,000.
Energy Independence: wants to end U.S. reliance on foreign energy by streamlining permits, reducing regulations, and expanding domestic oil, gas, coal and renewable production.
Eliminate the Department of Education and return control over how children are taught to states, local communities and parents.

positions.summary: Lists standing with President Trump to enforce reciprocal tariffs among his economic priorities.
positions.quote: America First Trade Policy: Stand with President Trump to enforce reciprocal tariffs that keep cheap imports out, bring manufacturing jobs back, and make sure American goods compete on the world stage.

positions.summary: Lists mass deportation of people in the country illegally as one of his top immigration priorities.
positions.quote: Mass Deportations: Nearly 70 million Americans voted for President Trump's plan to remove illegal aliens from our country and restore safety in American communities. Mass deportations mean mass deportations.

positions.summary: Says U.S. energy policy should prioritize ending what he calls "climate extremism" and expanding domestic fossil-fuel and other production rather than pursuing a faster transition away from fossil fuels.
positions.quote: American energy policy must prioritize independence, affordability, and efficiency. That means ending climate extremism, cutting red tape, and putting American producers back in charge of our resources.

positions.summary: Lists empowering law enforcement and backing the use of National Guard and military forces to assist police among his priorities on crime.
positions.quote: Empower Law Enforcement: Despite increased danger from Democrat rhetoric, America's police officers are working harder than ever and volunteering at higher rates because of the Trump effect. I stand with them and will always have their back.

positions.summary: Says families, not the federal government, should choose among public, private, charter or homeschool options for their children.
positions.quote: Champion School Choice: Families, not Washington, should decide the best path for their children, whether public, private, charter, or homeschool. Competition improves outcomes and ensures every child has a chance to succeed.

positions.summary: Says he fully supports the U.S. alliance with Israel against Hamas and other adversaries.
positions.quote: Stand with Israel: As a proud Jewish American, I fully support our alliance with Israel in the fight against Hamas, Al Qaeda, and all enemies of Western civilization.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and priorities above are drawn from Fine's official House issues pages (Economy, Immigration, Crime, Education, Energy, Foreign Policy). Federal roll-call votes, sponsored-bill lists and FEC finance totals for this sitting member are added by script.

candidates.name: Eric Yonce
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary over three opponents.

summary.text: Eric Yonce is the Democratic nominee for Florida's 6th Congressional District. Born in Florida and raised in the district, he spent over 20 years in retail management before entering real estate and starting a small business remodeling vintage Airstream trailers. He has not previously held office and describes himself as not a career politician.

background.text: Born in Hollywood, Florida, and raised in the 6th District; earned a high school diploma from North Marion High School.
Says his mother led the local Realtor Association and his father is a retired police officer.
Spent more than 20 years in big-box retail management.
Completed a 2,000+ mile thru-hike of the Appalachian Trail in 2022, then entered real estate and started a small business remodeling vintage Airstream trailers.
Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary with 32.1% in a four-candidate field.

priorities.text: Says he is not a career politician and wants to bring true representation to the district.
Opposes overdevelopment that strains resources, threatens the environment and increases flood risk; supports smart-growth policies.
Wants to address the rising cost of housing, energy and everyday expenses.

positions.summary: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey he says recent Supreme Court decisions have threatened a woman's right to choose and that protecting this liberty is essential.
positions.quote: Recent Supreme Court decisions have threatened a woman’s right to choose and could also endanger the right to marry whom one loves. Protecting these liberties is essential to preserving the principles of justice and equality that underpin our democracy.

statements.quote: Government should be doing more to address and adapt to climate change. We need to trust science and acknowledge the impacts of human-driven climate change that communities are already experiencing. That means investing in renewable energy, improving resilience, and making clean energy more accessible and affordable.
statements.context: In the WKMG ClickOrlando 2026 voter guide questionnaire

statements.quote: Growth should pay for growth so existing residents are not left covering the cost of overdevelopment.
statements.context: In the WKMG ClickOrlando 2026 voter guide questionnaire

statements.quote: Our international commitments, including our relationship with Israel and our financing of conflicts in the Middle East, require careful oversight to ensure that U.S. resources are being used responsibly and in ways that align with our national interests.
statements.context: In his 2025 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

candidates.researchNotes: Statements are from his 2025 Ballotpedia survey and WKMG ClickOrlando 2026 questionnaire. His campaign site's issues page did not load usable text.

candidates.name: Andrew Parrott
candidates.ballotNote: Libertarian primary was canceled; advanced unopposed.

summary.text: Andrew Parrott is the Libertarian Party nominee for Florida's 6th Congressional District and ran in the same seat's April 2025 special election. In a 2025 interview he said he worked about 20 years for one employer and had left the Republican Party for the Libertarian Party.

background.text: In a February 2025 AskFlagler interview, said he worked for roughly twenty years at a company whose health plan was self-insured and administered by Blue Cross Blue Shield.
Said he joined the Libertarian Party after having been "more closely associated with the Republicans for most of my life."
Ran as the Libertarian candidate in the April 1, 2025 special election, receiving 702 votes (0.4%); is the Libertarian nominee in 2026.

priorities.text: Portable health insurance not tied to a job, so people can choose and change plans.
Streamlining the Veterans Administration claims process, including mental health care.
Keeping Congress limited in the scope of what it is responsible for.

candidates.researchNotes: Statements are from a Feb. 2025 interview (2025 special election); he did not respond to the WKMG ClickOrlando 2026 voter guide. His campaign site has only a quotation and contact details.

statements.quote: I believe that the abortion issue is not something that can be solved legislatively. We can only really solve it culturally.

statements.quote: I'm very much anti-war and also anti-debt. If we allow Israel to go directly into debt with Lockheed Martin, I'd be much happier with things going that way.

candidates.name: Michael Gist
candidates.ballotNote: Unofficially withdrew from the race but remains on the November 3 general-election ballot.

summary.text: Michael Gist is a no-party-affiliation candidate for Florida's 6th Congressional District. He describes himself as a Marine Corps veteran, former public-school teacher, and lifelong Volusia County resident running on a proposal he calls 'Freedom Accounts.' Ballotpedia lists him as having withdrawn while remaining on the ballot.

background.text: Describes his family as lifelong residents of Volusia County for over 100 years; says his grandmother returned to Ormond Beach after working in New York in 1939.

Earned a high school diploma from Seabreeze High School, a graduate degree from National University (2002), a military citation from the Naval War College (2005), and a graduate degree from the University of Florida (2018), according to Ballotpedia.
Says he served 14 years in the U.S. Marine Corps and later taught in Volusia County public schools.

Is running as a self-described conservative Independent; his signature proposal, Freedom Accounts, would redirect government spending into personal investment accounts, according to his survey. Ballotpedia lists him as having withdrawn but still on the ballot.

priorities.text: Proposes 'Freedom Accounts,' a market-based plan redirecting government spending into personal investment accounts for education, homeownership, healthcare and long-term security.
Says he is running as an independent because he believes both major parties are dominated by elites rather than ordinary people.

statements.quote: I believe in a strong national defense, secure borders, and policies that keep America safe.
statements.context: In his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

statements.quote: I support real accountability, parental choice, and reforms that prioritize thinking skills and opportunity.
statements.context: In his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

candidates.researchNotes: Statements are from his 2026 Ballotpedia survey. Ballotpedia reports he unofficially withdrew but remains on the Nov. 3 ballot. His campaign site did not load (certificate error).

candidates.name: Alec Pavlik
candidates.ballotNote: Qualified as a write-in, no-party-affiliation candidate.

summary.text: Alec Pavlik is a write-in, no-party-affiliation candidate for Florida's 6th Congressional District. In his Ballotpedia survey he lists constitutional law, tax policy, and policies affecting natural rights as his areas of interest, along with copyright and corporate law.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Candidate Connection survey, or other public statements could be located for Pavlik (a web search returned nothing relevant).
